conventions.convention: Graphs are finite, simple, undirected and vertex-labeled; compared graphs use the same label set. Empty vertex sets are permitted.
Finite multisets are finitely supported nonnegative integer multiplicity functions; size counts multiplicity, and the empty multiset has size zero.

Message-passing maps are shared across compared graphs. Initialization depends only on labels; no vertex identities or graph-wide information enter before the final multiset readout. Depth may be zero.

WL starts at round zero with the original labels and uses canonical ordered pairs of center color and neighbor-color multiset. Distinguishability means unequal graph color multisets at some finite round.
The GIN definition imposes no injectivity on its finite MLPs or readout and makes no claim that a fixed finite architecture realizes an arbitrary injection.

Matching WL requires injectivity on the labels, neighbor multisets, center-state/aggregate pairs and final multisets encountered across the compared pair. Sum-code existence additionally uses a countable universe and fixed multiset-size bounds.

load_bearing.statement: Round zero colors are vertex labels; each next color is the ordered pair of the previous center color and neighbor-color multiset. Two graphs are distinguished at round t exactly when their graph color multisets differ.
Each layer aggregates the finite multiset of previous neighbor states and updates the previous center state using shared functions; graph output is a shared function of the final node-state multiset.

For a countable set X and M ≥ 0, there is a positive integer-valued map φ whose sum is injective on multisets of total multiplicity at most M. For every irrational ε, (c,S) ↦ (1+ε)φ(c)+Σ_{x∈S}φ(x) is injective on center/multiset pairs with the same bound.

For finite labeled graphs and a shared depth-K message-passing network, equal WL graph color multisets at every round 0 through K imply equal network graph outputs. Equivalently, network distinction implies WL distinction at some round at most K.

If WL distinguishes a finite labeled graph pair at round K, a shared depth-K message-passing network distinguishes it when initialization, aggregation, update and readout satisfy the stated injectivity conditions on the encountered inputs. The GIN sum-code clause assumes countability and fixed size bounds and does not assert arbitrary injection realization by a fixed finite MLP.
